premise: Rising from the slums of Bauru to win the World Cup at just 17 years old.
hook: He played barefoot with socks stuffed with rags because his family could not afford a real leather football.
key_facts: Born Edson Arantes do Nascimento in poverty in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Learned to play soccer using grapefruits and rolled-up rags in the streets.
Made his international debut for Brazil at age 16.
Scored two goals in the 1958 World Cup final to secure Brazil's first title.

premise: Refusing to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, sparking a pivotal movement against racial segregation.
hook: Her decision on a crowded city bus was a deliberate, courageous stand built on years of civil rights activism.
key_facts: Worked as a seamstress and served as secretary for the Montgomery chapter of the NAACP.
Was arrested on December 1, 1955, for violating Montgomery's segregation ordinances.
Triggered the 381-day Montgomery bus boycott organized by local Black leaders.
The boycott led to a U.S. Supreme Court ruling declaring segregated buses unconstitutional.

premise: Breaking the Soviet hegemony in chess to become India's first Grandmaster and a multi-time World Chess Champion.
hook: He learned chess from his mother in a small town in Tamil Nadu with virtually no local grandmaster infrastructure.
key_facts: Became India's first Grandmaster at the age of 18 in 1988.
Won the World Chess Championship five times across different formats.
Popularized chess significantly across India, inspiring a new generation of players.
Awarded India's second-highest civilian award, the Padma Vibhushan.

premise: Making his international cricket debut for India at just 16 years old against a lethal Pakistani pace attack.
hook: He walked out to bat against Waqar Younis and Wasim Akram with a bloodied nose after being hit by a bouncer, but refused to retire.
key_facts: Made his Test match debut against Pakistan in Karachi in November 1989 at age 16.
Scored 100 international centuries over a 24-year career.
Became the first player to score a double century in a Men's One Day International.
Awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor.

premise: A self-taught mathematical genius from India mailing his raw theorems across the world to Cambridge in search of recognition.
hook: Almost every top British mathematician threw his strange formulas in the trash—until one man opened the envelope.
key_facts: Grew up in Erode, Tamil Nadu, with almost no formal training in pure mathematics.
Independently compiled nearly 3,900 mathematical results and identities.
Mailed letters containing his complex theorems to prominent Cambridge mathematicians in 1913.
Invited to Trinity College, Cambridge, by G.H. Hardy, leading to groundbreaking joint publications.

premise: Keeping his entire 28-man crew alive for nearly two years after their ship was crushed by Antarctic pack ice.
hook: His ship was crushed and sunk by Antarctic ice, stranding 28 men on floating floes with no way to call for help.
key_facts: Led the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition aboard the Endurance, which became trapped in ice in 1915.
The ship sank, forcing the crew to camp on drifting ice floes for months.
Sailed an 22-foot lifeboat 800 miles across treacherous seas to South Georgia Island for rescue.
Successfully rescued every single member of his crew without a single loss of life.

premise: Writing portions of a fantasy manuscript in Edinburgh cafes while dealing with extreme financial hardship.
hook: She wrote her first blockbuster manuscript in public cafes simply because it was warmer than her unheated apartment.
key_facts: Lived as a single mother relying on state benefits in Edinburgh, Scotland.
Completed the first manuscript of the fantasy novel over several years during her daughter's nap times.
Rejected by a dozen publishing houses before Bloomsbury accepted the manuscript in 1996.
The book went on to launch one of the most successful literary and cinematic franchises in history.

premise: Inventing a tactile reading and writing system as a teenager after losing his sight in a childhood accident.
hook: Blinded at age three by a leather tool in his father's workshop, he refused to let darkness limit human knowledge.
key_facts: Blinded in his right eye at age three due to an infection caused by an accidental puncture.
Attended the Royal Institution for Blind Youth in Paris, where books were extremely rare and hard to read.
Adapted a military 'night writing' code of raised dots into a streamlined six-dot alphabet by age 15.
The system was eventually adopted globally, transforming education for visually impaired people.
